ayahOccurrences.text: وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ أَن يَقْتُلَ مُؤْمِنًا إِلَّا خَطَـًٔا ۚ وَمَن قَتَلَ مُؤْمِنًا خَطَـًٔا فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُّؤْمِنَةٍ وَدِيَةٌ مُّسَلَّمَةٌ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَن يَصَّدَّقُوا۟ ۚ فَإِن كَانَ مِن قَوْمٍ عَدُوٍّ لَّكُمْ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُّؤْمِنَةٍ ۖ وَإِن كَانَ مِن قَوْمٍۭ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُم مِّيثَٰقٌ فَدِيَةٌ مُّسَلَّمَةٌ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِۦ وَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُّؤْمِنَةٍ ۖ فَمَن لَّمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ تَوْبَةً مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا

entries.label: أسْلَمَ
entries.definitionHtml:
أسْلَمَ ʾaslama I [v. IV, intrans.]

1 to surrender, to submit, to devote oneself

(3:83) أَفَغَيْرَ دِينِ اللَّهِ يَبْغُونَ وَلَهُ أَسْلَمَ مَنْ فِى السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ طَوْعًا وَكَرْهًا do they seek anything other than submission to God?, Everyone in the heavens and earth submits to Him willingly or unwillingly

2 to resign oneself, to come to accept

(37:103) فَلَمَّا أَسْلَمَا وَتَلَّهُ لِلْجَبِينِ so when they came to accept and he laid him upon his forehead

3 to profess the religion of Islam, to become a Muslim

(49:17) يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ أَسْلَمُوا they count it as a favour to you [Prophet], that they have become Muslims II [v. IV, trans.] *

(2:112) مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ لِلَّهِ he who submits his whole being to God [lit. face].

entries.label: إسْلام
entries.definitionHtml:
إسْلام ʾislām I [n.] total surrender

(3:19) إِنَّ الدِّينَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الإِسْلاَمُ True Religion, in God’s eyes, is total surrender [to Him]

2 [with the definite article الإسْلام ʾal‐ʾislām] the religion of Islam

(5:3) الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ الإِسْلاَمَ دِينًا today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My blessing upon you, and sanctioned for you Islam [the total submission to God] as religion II [v. n.] (act of) surrendering, submitting

(9:74) وَلَقَدْ قَالُوا كَلِمَةَ الْكُفْرِ وَكَفَرُوا بَعْدَ إِسْلاَمِهِمْ but they certainly did speak the word of disbelief and became disbelievers after having submitted.

entries.label: تَسْليم
entries.definitionHtml:
تَسْليم taslım [v. n. of v. II, adverbially used]

1 surrendering, yielding

(4:65) ثُمَّ لاَ يَجِدُوا فِى أَنْفُسِهِمْ حَرَجًا مِمَّا قَضَيْتَ وَيُسَلِّمُوا تَسْلِيمًا and then they will find no constraint in their hearts regarding your judgement, and yield completely

2 greeting with the words ‘peace’

(33:56) صَلُّوا عَلَيْهِ وَسَلِّمُوا تَسْلِيمًا bless him [the Prophet] and salute him with greetings of peace (or, surrender yourselves completely to his guidance).

entries.label: سالِمون
entries.definitionHtml:
سالِمون sālimūn[pl. of act. part. سالِم sālim] safe and sound, not threatened

(68:43) وَقَدْ كَانُوا يُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى السُّجُودِ وَهُمْ سَالِمُونَ they were invited to prostrate themselves when they were safe [but refused].

entries.label: سَلام
entries.definitionHtml:
سَلام salām I [n.]

1 peace

(5:16) يَهْدِي بِهِ اللَّهُ مَنِ اتَّبَعَ رِضْوَانَهُ سُبُلَ السَّلاَمِ With which God guides those who follow what pleases Him to the paths of peace; *

(59:23) الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ السَّلاَمُ the King, the Holy One, the Source of Peace; *

(6:127) دار السلام Paradise [lit. the house of peace]

2 safety, security

(21:69) قُلْنَا يَانَارُ كُونِي بَرْدًا وَسَلاَمًا عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ [but] We said, ‘Fire, be coolness and safety for Abraham’

3 greeting of peace

(56:91) فَسَلاَمٌ لَكَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ الْيَمِينِ and so ‘Peace be on you’ [will be said to you] by the companions on the Right; *

(6:54) سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ ‘Peace be upon you’ II [adverbially]

1 greeting of peace to you

(51:25) إِذْ دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ فَقَالُوا سَلاَمًا they went in to see him and said, ‘greetings of peace’; *

(56:26) إِلاَّ قِيلا سَلاَمًا سَلاَمًا only agreeable speech [will they hear in Paradise] [lit. but a saying of ‘Peace, peace’]

2 being clear, or quit, of

(25:63) وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ الْجَاهِلُونَ قَالُوا سَلاَمًا and when the ignorant speak to them, they say: ‘We have nothing to do with you [lit. are quit of you]’ (or, they say ‘in Peace’) .

entries.label: سَليم
entries.definitionHtml:
سَليم salım [quasi‐act. part.]

1 pure, wholesome, sound, free of evil

(26:89) إِلاَّ مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ except for the one who comes before God with a pure heart

2 sick, heavy, troubled (in one interpretation of 37:84) إِذْ جَاءَ رَبَّهُ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ when he came to his Lord with a troubled (or, a pure) heart.

entries.label: سَلَم
entries.definitionHtml:
سَلَم salam I [n.] peace, end of hostility

(4:90) فَإِنِ اعْتَزَلُوكُمْ فَلَمْ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ وَأَلْقَوْا إِلَيْكُمُ السَّلَمَ فَمَا جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ سَبِيلًا so if they leave you alone and do not fight you, and offer you peace, then God gives you no way against them II [quasi‐pass. part.] wholly devoted to, wholly belonging to

(39:29) ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلا رَجُلا فِيهِ شُرَكَاءُ مُتَشَاكِسُونَ وَرَجُلا سَلَمًا لِرَجُلٍ God sets forth a parable–of a man belonging to partners who are at odds with one another, and a man belonging wholly to one man.

entries.label: سَلَّم
entries.definitionHtml:
سَلَّم sallama I [v. II, intrans.]

1 to submit to a verdict, to give in

(4:65) ثُمَّ لاَ يَجِدُوا فِى أَنْفُسِهِمْ حَرَجًا مِمَّا قَضَيْتَ وَيُسَلِّمُوا تَسْلِيمًا and then they will find no constraint in their hearts regarding your judgement, and yield completely

2 [with prep. عَلَى] to greet, to salute

(24:27) وَتُسَلِّمُوا عَلَى أَهْلِهَا and greet their inhabitants; *

(33:56) صَلُّوا عَلَيْهِ وَسَلِّمُوا تَسْلِيمًا bless him [the Prophet] and salute him with greetings of peace (or, surrender yourselves completely to his guidance)

3 [with no notion of an obj.] to spare [from a bad outcome], to bail out, to save the day

(8:43) وَلَوْ أَرَاكَهُمْ كَثِيرًا لَفَشِلْتُمْ وَلَتَنَازَعْتُمْ فِى الأَمْرِ وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ سَلَّمَ had He shown them to you as many, you would certainly have lost heart and disputed about the matter, but God saved the day II [v. II, trans.] to hand over

(2:233) وَإِنْ أَرَدْتُمْ أَنْ تَسْتَرْضِعُوا أَوْلاَدَكُمْ فَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذَا سَلَّمْتُمْ مَا ءَاتَيْتُمْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ and if you wish to have your children suckled [by someone other than the mother] there will be no blame attached to you, provided you pay an agreed amount in a fair manner.

entries.label: سَلْم
entries.definitionHtml:
سَلْم salm [n.] peace

(8:61) وَإِنْ جَنَحُوا لِلسَّلْمِ فَاجْنَحْ لَهَا but if they lean towards peace, then lean towards it [as well].

entries.label: سُلَّم
entries.definitionHtml:
سُلَّم sullam [n.] ladder

(52:38) أَمْ لَهُمْ سُلَّمٌ يَسْتَمِعُونَ فِيهِ or do they have a ladder from which they [are able to] eavesdrop?

entries.label: سِلْم
entries.definitionHtml:
سِلْم silm [n.] peace; self‐surrender (a large number of commentators, however, interpret this word as meaning ‘the religion of Islam’ in spite of contextual incompatibility)

(2:208) يَاأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا ادْخُلُوا فِى السِّلْمِ كَافَّةً you who believe, enter wholeheartedly into complete submission to God.

entries.label: مُسْتَسْلِمون
entries.definitionHtml:
مُسْتَسْلِمون mustaslimūn [pl. of مُسْتَسْلِم mustaslim; act. part.] those submitting, surrendering

(37:26) بَلْ هُمُ الْيَوْمَ مُسْتَسْلِمُونَ no indeed!, they will be in complete submission on this Day.

entries.label: مُسْلِم
entries.definitionHtml:
مُسْلِم muslim[act. part.]

1 one who submits [to God]

(2:133) نَعْبُدُ إِلَهَكَ وَإِلَهَ ءَابَائِكَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ إِلَهًا وَاحِدًا وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ we will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael and Isaac, one single God–we submit ourselves to Him

2 one who professes the faith of Islam

(22:78) هُوَ سَمَّاكُمُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَفِي هَذَا He has called you Muslims–both in the past and in this [Book]

3 one showing obedience

(27:38) أَيُّكُمْ يَأْتِينِي بِعَرْشِهَا قَبْلَ أَنْ يَأْتُونِي مُسْلِمِينَ which of you can bring me her throne before they come to me in obedience [to my bidding]?
